info.title: SynapseDesk API
info.description:
The REST surface of the SynapseDesk gateway. Every response is wrapped in the standard envelope — `{ success, statusCode, message, warning, data }` on success and `{ success, statusCode, path, timestamp, error }` on failure — so the schema shown for a route describes the whole body, not just its payload.

## Caching and staleness

Some reads are served from a shared cache. An operation that is cached says so in its `x-cache` extension: `{ scope, ttlSeconds, varyBy }`. Everything else is computed per request.

**A cached read can be stale for at most its TTL, and usually far less.** Cache entries are keyed by `(tenant, scope, parameters)` rather than by URL, so a write CAN find and evict them — a mutation drops its whole scope for that tenant before it answers, and changes that originate elsewhere in the system (a WebSocket message, a background job, another service) evict through domain events. The TTL is the backstop for a writer nobody has enumerated, not the mechanism.

`varyBy` says what the entry depends on. `tenant` means every member of your organization shares one answer. `caller` means the answer is filtered by what you can see — `GET /documents` is scoped to your departments — so it is shared only with people whose visibility matches yours.

**The one entry with no eviction is `GET /permissions`.** The permission catalogue is seeded and changes on deploy, so there is no request that could invalidate it; its one-hour TTL is the whole story.

**Tickets, messages and notifications are never cached**, and neither is `GET /notifications/unread-count` — the WebSocket pushes that authoritatively, so polling it is the thing to remove rather than the thing to speed up.

### GraphQL

There is **no response cache** on `/graphql`. A GraphQL response key would be a hash of the query document, and nothing in such a key says which entities the answer contains — so no write could ever find it, and a cached response would be stale for its full TTL no matter what changed. What is cached instead are the individual entities behind edges (`assignee`, `author`, `sender`, `actor`, `department`), keyed one per entity and evicted precisely when that entity changes.

### Your half

After a mutation, refetch or update your own store rather than trusting the next query to be fresh. A mutation returns fresh data to its own caller; another tab holding a rendered list is the server's problem only up to the eviction it just performed. Apollo Client does this by default with normalized cache updates.

envelope._about: Applied to every ApiResponse* wrapper: the same envelope on every success.
envelope.warning: A non-fatal advisory about a request that otherwise succeeded — a degraded search, a partially-applied bulk operation. Null when there is nothing to say.

GET /health.description: Checks NOTHING external, deliberately. A liveness probe that failed on a dependency outage would get every container restarted, which repairs none of it. Served outside the `/api/v1` prefix: an orchestrator is not an API client and cannot follow a version migration.

GET /health/ready.summary: Readiness — should traffic reach THIS instance?
GET /health/ready.description: `ready` is false only while this instance is draining. Redis is REPORTED under `dependencies` and does not gate: every instance shares it, so gating would turn a Redis outage into a total one, while the routes keep serving without it. Peer gRPC health is REPORTED under `peers` and deliberately does not gate: every instance sees the same peer down, so gating would remove all of them and turn one service outage into a total one. A partial outage should look partial. Returns 503 when not ready — a probe reads the status line, not the body.

GET /version.description: Three fields and no more — version, commit SHA, build time. Node version, dependency lists and environment names are deliberately absent: they turn a support aid into a reconnaissance endpoint on a public route, and none of them answer the question this exists for.

POST /api/v1/webhooks/email/resend.description: **Not a public endpoint despite carrying no security scheme.** Every request is authenticated by a Standard Webhooks signature over the exact raw bytes of the body, in `svix-signature` with `svix-id` and `svix-timestamp` — a claim OpenAPI has no way to express. Called only by Resend; no client should ever reach it. Answers **200 for every outcome except a bad signature and a retryable fetch failure**, including mail this system deliberately drops: an unknown tenant token, a sender whose domain is not permitted, a mail that fails validation. A non-2xx tells Resend to retry for hours, so one misconfigured mail rule would become a retry loop; a 503 is answered only when fetching the mail failed in a way a retry can fix.

POST /api/v1/webhooks/stripe.description: **Not a public endpoint despite carrying no security scheme.** Every request is authenticated by Stripe's `stripe-signature` header, computed as an HMAC over the exact raw bytes of the body — a stronger claim than a bearer token, and one OpenAPI cannot describe. Always answers 200, even for an event this system could not apply: Stripe retries on any non-2xx, so a 500 for an unmappable price id would turn one config typo into an escalating retry storm. The only non-2xx is a signature failure.

DELETE /api/v1/platform/organizations/{i.summary: Release an assigned plan (or dry-run it)

AcceptInvitationDto.deviceName.description:
Labels the session this call creates, in the user's active-device list.

Optional: the client sends what it can identify itself as, and a session
with no label is still a session.

ActivateTwoFactorDto.deviceName.description: The new session's device label, used only when enabling through the sign-in challenge signs you in.

AddDepartmentMembersDto.isPrimary.description:
Makes THIS department primary for every user in the batch. A user has at
most one primary, so setting it here demotes whichever they had.

AddDepartmentMembersResponseDto.updatedC.description: Existing memberships whose `isPrimary`/assigner were refreshed instead.

AgentAnalyticsResponseDto.dataThrough.description:
**The last day the underlying rollups cover**, `YYYY-MM-DD`,
or `null` when nothing has ever been rolled up.

This endpoint spans more than one service, so it reports the STALEST leg:
a composed answer is only as fresh as its oldest input, and reporting the
freshest would let one healthy service vouch for a broken one.

AgentAnalyticsResponseDto.unavailable.description: Which legs could not be reached. Empty when everything answered.

AgentStatResponseDto.draftAcceptance.description: From the AI ledger. null when that leg was unavailable.

AgentStatResponseDto.fullName.description: null when the id could not be resolved — a deleted user, or a lookup that failed.

AiClassificationResponseDto.suggestedPri.description:
Null when the model named something that is not a priority.

The value crosses two hops: rag-service (Python) answers a bare string, and
ticket-service narrows it there — at the one boundary where it is genuinely
foreign — before putting it on `ClassifyTicketResponse` as a real enum. So a
`MEDIUM-HIGH` or a translated label arrives here as null rather than as a
suggestion the UI would render and no agent could apply.

AiDraftResponseDto.generationId.description:
The `ai_generations` row this draft came from.

**Hand it back as `generatedFromId` when posting the reply.** That is what
lets ticket-service record the draft as ACCEPTED or EDITED; omit it and the
hourly sweep records it as DISCARDED instead.

AiSuggestionsResponseDto.degraded.description:
`LEXICAL_ONLY` when the budget could not confirm room for a generation —
the workspace is at its AI allowance, or the quota counter was unreadable.
Then `nextSteps` is empty because the model was never called, and
`articles` came from keyword search. `null` on a normal answer, where an
empty `nextSteps` means the model had nothing to add.

Read it before rendering an empty `nextSteps`: without it, a client shows
"no suggestions" where the truth is "allowance used".

AiUsageResponseDto.aiModelTier.description:
`FAST` | `QUALITY`, or null.

The wire field was a bare `string` while `billing.proto` spelled the same
fact as `AiModelTier` — drift rather than a decision, and it is an enum on
both now. Null only for UNSPECIFIED, which means auth-service returned no
entitlement.

AiUsageResponseDto.byPurpose.description: **The per-purpose split is the point** — where the budget actually goes.

ApplyPlanResponseDto.evaluatedDimensions.description:
Which limits this run actually checked.

A dimension absent from the list was NOT evaluated, and `overLimitCount`
says nothing about it — render it as unknown rather than as zero affected.

AssignTicketDto.departmentId.description:
Required, not inferred from the assignee's primary department.

Inferring it would put the ticket wherever that agent happens to sit, which
is wrong the moment someone belongs to two teams — and it would make the
queue a ticket lands in depend on a fact about a PERSON rather than a
decision about the WORK. Both ids are validated against auth-service before
anything is written.

AssignTicketDto.reason.description:
Why it moved. Absent means the service decides from context: `INITIAL` for
a first assignment, `MANUAL` for any later one.

AssignmentResponseDto.assignedById.description:
Who assigned it. Always a person.

Was `string | null`; the null had no writer — `writeAssignment` is the only
one and takes an actor (known-gaps #12). Part of the pre-client clearing —
see `PaginationDto`.

AttachmentResponseDto.fileUrl.description: An internal object path today; a signed URL once storage-service lands.

AttachmentResponseDto.messageId.description: Null for a file on the ticket's opening, which has no message.

AttachmentResponseDto.ticketId.description: The ticket the file belongs to, through its message or directly.

AuditLogResponseDto.action.description:
What happened, as an `AuditAction`.

`null` for a row whose action THIS build cannot name — only reachable
mid-rolling-deploy, and a client is better told "unknown" than handed a
value its union does not contain.

AuditLogResponseDto.metadata.description:
Parsed back into an object for the client.

It crosses gRPC as a JSON string because the shape differs per action; a
typed proto message could only be a `map<string, string>`, which would
flatten every nested value in the before/after diff.

AuditLogResponseDto.organizationId.description: null for a PLATFORM act — the event belongs to the platform, not a tenant.

AuditLogResponseDto.userId.description: null for system and cron actors, which have no user acting for them.

AuthenticateTwoFactorDto.rememberDevice.description: Skip the code on this device for a while. Ignored for a Super Admin.

BackfillJobDto.reason.description:
**Mandatory.** A backfill rewrites numbers somebody may already have acted
on, and "why" is the only part of that a reader cannot reconstruct
afterwards from the rows themselves.

BackupCodesResponseDto.backupCodes.description: Shown once. Only hashes are stored.

BillingEventPointResponseDto.eventType.description:
**A string, and it carries two vocabularies.**

In `points` it is Stripe's (`invoice.payment_failed`); in
`currentlyOffboarded` it is `organization.offboarded`, which this system
invented. A client writing a `switch` over this field will meet both.

BillingEventsResponseDto.currentlyOffboa.description:
Tenants CURRENTLY offboarded, bucketed by the day they were offboarded — a
different ending from a cancellation.

**Named for the state rather than the event, deliberately.** It is derived
from `organizations.deleted_at`, which a restore clears, so restoring a
tenant removes it from every past range. As an event count that would be a
series rewriting its own history; as a projection of current state it
behaves as named. A stable churn line needs the audit log, which lives in
another service.

BillingEventsResponseDto.observedEventTy.description:
The event types actually seen in this range.

A type that has never arrived is visibly absent here rather than reported
as a zero — and which types arrive at all is the Stripe endpoint's
`enabled_events`, which nothing in this repository configures.

ChangePasswordResponseDto.revokedSession.description: Other devices signed out by the change. The caller keeps this session.

ChangePlanDto.priceId.description:
Both ids, and they must agree.

Sending only the price would let a caller name Pro's plan and Starter's
price; sending only the plan would charge them for a price the plan does
not own. The endpoint refuses a mismatch rather than picking one.

CitationResponseDto.pageNumber.description:
The page this citation points at, or `null` when the source document has no
pages — a pasted text file, an HTML article. Never faked as 1.

CitationResponseDto.vectorPointId.description: The retrieval key the citation resolves through.

ConfirmAttachmentDto.objectPath.description:
Echoed back from the presign response.

Not shape-validated here on purpose: ticket-service passes it to
storage-service, which checks it against the PendingUpload it recorded — a
real authorization check rather than a syntactic one. A regex here would
only reject well-formed paths that were never authorized, which is exactly
the case the real check catches better.

ConfirmAvatarDto.objectPath.description:
The path the presign step returned, echoed back.

Not validated as a URL or a shape here, on purpose: storage-service checks
it against the PendingUpload it recorded, which is a real authorization
check rather than a syntactic one. A regex here would only reject
well-formed paths that were never authorized — the exact case the real
check catches better.

ConfirmDocumentDto.isOrganizationWide.description:
Defaults TRUE, matching RDM Table 17.

The permissive default is deliberate and worth stating: a knowledge base
whose documents defaulted to invisible would look broken to everyone who
did not also configure departments, and the failure mode of the other
default — a document nobody can find — is a support ticket rather than a
disclosure. Restricting is then an explicit act.

ConfirmDocumentDto.objectPath.description: The object path, echoed back from the presign response.

ConfirmDocumentDto.ocrLanguages.description:
ISO 639-1 codes for OCR, if the uploader knows them.

An advanced field: leave it empty unless the upload is known to be scanned.
`[]` and absent are the same thing, and the parser falls back to `eng`.

CreateAuditLogExportDto.filters.description: `action`, `resourceType`, `userId` — refused per kind at the service.

CreateDepartmentDto.description.description: Markdown is accepted and preserved unmodified — this field is never sanitized, escaped or transformed beyond trimming. Renderers MUST disable raw HTML: markdown permits inline HTML, none is stripped here, and a renderer that passes it through turns this field into stored XSS.

CreateExportDto.filters.description:
Per-kind predicates the three kinds do not share.

Validated at the SERVICE against `EXPORT_FILTER_KEYS`, not here: the
allowed keys differ per kind, and a DTO cannot see which kind it carries
without splitting into three. An unknown key is refused rather than stored
and ignored — a filter the caller believes applied and that silently did
not is the failure this shape is most exposed to.

CreateGlobalRoleDto.description.description: Markdown is accepted and preserved unmodified — this field is never sanitized, escaped or transformed beyond trimming. Renderers MUST disable raw HTML: markdown permits inline HTML, none is stripped here, and a renderer that passes it through turns this field into stored XSS.

CreateMessageDto.attachments.description:
Objects already uploaded, bound to this message as it is created


**This is the ordering that makes a first-turn attachment readable.**
Presign then confirm-against-a-message meant the row could only exist after
the message did, while `invokeAi` runs during the create — so the very
screenshot the question was about arrived a moment too late to be seen.

A path that fails its confirm comes back in `skippedAttachments` and the
message is still created, and that is why that is the only safe outcome.

CreateMessageDto.content.description: Markdown is accepted and preserved unmodified — this field is never sanitized, escaped or transformed beyond trimming. Renderers MUST disable raw HTML: markdown permits inline HTML, none is stripped here, and a renderer that passes it through turns this field into stored XSS.

CreateMessageDto.generatedFromId.description:
The `ai_generations` row this reply came from — `AiDraftResponseDto`'s
`generationId`, handed back.

Send it when posting an AI-drafted reply so the draft is recorded ACCEPTED
or EDITED rather than DISCARDED. Absent for an ordinary reply.

CreateMessageDto.invokeAi.description:
Ask for an AI draft after this message lands.

Two writes, never one: the draft can fail without losing what the human
typed. Today it always fails — `rag-service` does not exist — and the
caller's own message still commits, which is exactly the behaviour that
has to survive Domain C shipping.

CreateMessageDto.isInternalNote.description:
Agent-only, enforced in ticket-service rather than by a route permission:
the route itself must stay open to end users, who post ordinary replies
through it.

CreateMessageResponseDto.skippedAttachme.description:
File NAMES, never object paths and never contents — the same rule the AI's
own skipped list follows, and for the same reason: a user reads this.

CreateTicketResponseDto.skippedAttachmen.description:
File NAMES, never object paths: a path that failed its confirm (expired,
not the caller's, not an attachment). The ticket is created regardless.

CreatePlatformOrganizationDto.slug.description: Trimmed and lowercased first, then lowercase letters, digits and hyphens only, so `ACME-Corp` is stored as `acme-corp`.

CreateRoleDto.description.description: Markdown is accepted and preserved unmodified — this field is never sanitized, escaped or transformed beyond trimming. Renderers MUST disable raw HTML: markdown permits inline HTML, none is stripped here, and a renderer that passes it through turns this field into stored XSS.

CreateTicketDto.authorId.description:
Raising a ticket on behalf of an end user. Only an agent may (a super
admin, or a holder of `ticket.read.all` or `ticket.message.moderate`);
anyone else naming someone other than themselves gets a 403.

Absent means "the caller", which is the ordinary case and needs no
validation because the id comes from a verified token. When present it is
checked against auth-service before the insert — there is no foreign key
that could do it, since `users` lives in another database.

CreateTicketDto.attachments.description:
Files already uploaded through `POST /tickets/attachments/upload-url`,
bound to the ticket's opening as it is created. A path that fails its
confirm comes back in `skippedAttachments`; the ticket is created
regardless.

CreateTicketDto.description.description: Markdown is accepted and preserved unmodified — this field is never sanitized, escaped or transformed beyond trimming. Renderers MUST disable raw HTML: markdown permits inline HTML, none is stripped here, and a renderer that passes it through turns this field into stored XSS.

CreateTicketExportDto.filters.description: `status`, `priority`, `assigneeId` — refused per kind at the service.

CreateWebhookEndpointDto.eventTypes.description:
At least one — an endpoint subscribed to nothing is refused at creation,
never created silently useless, and an empty list never means "all".

CurrentUserResponseDto.isSuperAdmin.description: A platform Super Admin, who has no organization and uses the console.

CurrentUserResponseDto.permissionCodes.description: Every permission code the caller holds, granted through their roles.

CurrentUserResponseDto.hasPassword.description:
Whether the account has a password. A Google-only one doesn't, and sets
one through `POST /auth/password/forgot`.

DeleteOrganizationDto.reason.description:
Required. Offboarding is finalized by a Super Admin who was not in the
room, and "why did Acme leave?" is the first thing they will ask.

DepartmentResponseDto.deletedAt.description: Non-null only on a soft-deleted row.

DeviceTokenResponseDto.lastUsedAt.description: Null until the first successful push — how stale this device is.

DeviceTokenResponseDto.platform.description: `IOS` | `ANDROID` | `WEB` or `null` if the platform is not recognized.

DocumentAnalyticsResponseDto.citationAcc.description: Citation accuracy from `ai_response_feedbacks` — the other service's leg.

DocumentAnalyticsResponseDto.neverRetrie.description: **Two DIFFERENT findings** (RDM Table 27), never merged into one list.

DocumentChunkResponseDto.vectorPointId.description: null until the Qdrant upsert has written it back — i.e. not yet retrievable.

DocumentFlagResponseDto.documentTitle.description: The flagged document's title, joined in so the list reads as a worklist.

DocumentFlagResponseDto.flagType.description:
What kind of attention this document needs, or `null` when the value is one
this build does not recognise — the same nullability
{@link DocumentResponseDto.status} carries, and for the same reason.

DocumentFlagResponseDto.resolution.description: `null` while the flag is open, which is what an open flag sends.

DocumentFlagResponseDto.resolvedById.description: A bare id — the gateway does not hydrate it into a user.

DocumentResponseDto.fileType.description:
The stored EXTENSION — `pdf`, `txt`, `md` — never the MIME type.

`bin` is a real member: any accepted type with no extension mapping is
filed under it, as is a value this build does not recognise.

DocumentResponseDto.fileUrl.description: An internal object path today; a signed URL only via `/download`.

DocumentResponseDto.ocrLanguages.description:
ISO 639-1 codes the uploader declared for OCR.

`[]` means "not specified" — never `null`, so absent and empty are one
value all the way to the client.

DraftCitationResponseDto.pageNumber.description:
The page this citation points at, or `null` when the source document has no
pages — a pasted text file, an HTML article. Never faked as 1.

DunningTenantResponseDto.pastDueSince.description:
When it went past due: its status's last change. Null for an
organization whose status changed before that was recorded.

DunningTenantResponseDto.updatedAt.description:
When the tenant row last changed — **not when it went past due**.

`organizations` has no status-change timestamp, so this is the closest
available fact and a rename or a quota edit moves it. Rendering it as a
dunning age would be a confidently wrong number.

ExportResponseDto.downloadUrl.description:
Present only while READY, and minted per request.

A signed URL to a tenant's full ticket history is a credential, so it is
never stored — which is also why polling twice yields two different URLs.

ExportResponseDto.rollupComputedAt.description:
The newest rollup run behind the file — the disputed-number guard.

Two people exporting "last quarter" a week apart can see whether the data
was recomputed between them rather than guessing.

FeedbackResponseDto.citationAccurate.description: null means "not assessed", NOT "assessed and wrong".

FinancePlanMixResponseDto.seatsAllocated.description: Summed from what tenants HOLD, so pinned and overridden grants count.

FinancePlanMixResponseDto.subscribers.description:
Live subscribers — **not** `SubscriptionPlanResponseDto.subscriberCount`.

That one is unfiltered and counts soft-deleted tenants, because
`DELETE /platform/plans/:id` reads it to refuse retiring a plan somebody
still points at and an offboarded tenant can be restored. This one excludes
them, because an offboarded tenant is not a subscriber and the same
response's `tenants.total` excludes them too.

FinanceRevenueResponseDto.computedAt.description: When the JOB read Stripe — never when this endpoint answered.

FinanceRevenueResponseDto.currency.description: NULL when there are no active subscriptions to take one from.

FinanceRevenueResponseDto.estimatedMrr.description: Smallest currency unit. Annual prices divided by twelve.

FinanceRevenueResponseDto.excludes.description:
The caveats, traveling with the number.

On the wire deliberately: a field called `mrr` gets quoted in a meeting,
and a caveat that lives in a document nobody opens beside the chart is not
a caveat. Present on every response, including the ones with no number.

FinanceSnapshotResponseDto.generatedAt.description: When this response was assembled; see `revenue.computedAt` for the snapshot's age.

FinanceTenantCountsResponseDto.byStatus.description:
Keyed by status, so a new status needs no new field.

**`ACTIVE` here is not `activeSubscriptions` below.** The Stripe status
mapping folds `trialing` into `ACTIVE`, and the revenue estimate counts
`status: 'active'` subscriptions only. Two populations, one adjective —
subtracting one from the other produces a number that means nothing.

GenerateDraftDto.instruction.description:
An optional steer from the agent — "shorter", "offer the refund".

Absent means "draft from the thread alone", which is the ordinary case.
Bounded because this is user text that reaches a model prompt: an unbounded
field here is an unbounded token bill, quite apart from what someone could
try to write into it.

GoogleSignInDto.idToken.description:
The Firebase ID token the browser obtained from the Google flow.

Safe to accept from the body precisely because it is not trusted:
auth-service verifies its signature against Google's public keys, so a
forged value fails there rather than being believed here.

InboundAddressResponseDto.inboundAddress.description: Publish this as the tenant’s support address. Rotating it issues a new one and stops the previous address routing immediately.

IngestionJobResponseDto.bullmqJobId.description: Empty until the worker has queued it.

IngestionJobResponseDto.errorCode.description:
Why a `FAILED` attempt failed, as a reader can act on it: too long, no
readable text, OCR unavailable, the AI provider failed, or other.
`errorLog` stays the detail. `null` on an attempt that hasn't failed.

IngestionJobResponseDto.failedStage.description: The stage a `FAILED` attempt was in. `null` on one that hasn't failed.

IngestionJobResponseDto.processedAt.description: `null` while the attempt is still running.

IngestionJobResponseDto.status.description: `null` only if the peer sent a member this build does not know.

IngestionJobResponseDto.waitingReason.description:
Why a `QUEUED` attempt waits: `AI_ALLOWANCE` when it was put back because
the organization's AI allowance ran out mid-run; it starts again by itself
once the allowance resets or the plan changes. `null` is an ordinary queue.

InvitationPreviewRowResponseDto.unknownR.description: Reported even on an OK row: these are skipped at redemption, not fatal.

InviteUserDto.roleIds.description:
PROPOSALS, resolved at redemption rather than now. A role deleted during
the 7-day window is skipped and reported, never fatal.

InvoiceResponseDto.status.description:
**STRIPE's** invoice status — `draft`, `open`, `paid`, `uncollectible`,
`void` — passed through from a live API read, so it stays a `string`.

The one status field on this surface that must NOT be narrowed. An enum
over a third party's vocabulary turns a value they add into a runtime
surprise on a page about money; a foreign literal is stored and forwarded
as it arrives, the same rule `SubscriptionPlanPrice.interval` follows.
Written here rather than only in the proto because this is the third time
the question has been asked about a Stripe status field.

JobHealthResponseDto.degraded.description:
True when ANY expected job is unhealthy — the single field a monitor can
alert on without knowing the job list.

JobHealthResponseDto.unavailable.description: Which legs could not be reached, so a partial answer is legible as one.

JobRunStatusResponseDto.health.description:
How this row is doing — see {@link JobHealth} for the five values.

Computed here rather than stored, because the judgement needs the list of
jobs this build EXPECTS: a job that has never run has no row, and a reader
that only looks at the rows it finds reports nothing wrong.

JobRunStatusResponseDto.service.description: Which service owns the schedule — the two have separate databases.

KnowledgeArticleBlockResponseDto.pageNum.description: `null` for formats with no pages — never faked as 1.

KnowledgeArticleDetailResponseDto.hasUni.description:
True when some of the source could not be read.

The blocks are then less than the document, and nothing in them shows it —
`chunkIndex` is contiguous over what survived, so there is no gap to
notice. Render it as a notice rather than hiding the article: 197 readable
pages beat none, which is the trade indexing already made.

KnowledgeArticleDetailResponseDto.meta.description:
Describes the BLOCK range, not a page of articles.

A whole document is unbounded — a 200-page handbook is hundreds of blocks —
so the detail view pages through the text rather than returning it whole.

KnowledgeArticleDetailResponseDto.passag.description:
When the request named a `passage`: its index within `blocks`, for the
reader to highlight and scroll to. `null` otherwise.

KnowledgeArticleResponseDto.chunkCount.description: The only reading-length signal on this response, `fileSizeBytes` being absent.

KnowledgeAskResponseDto.generationId.description:
The `ai_generations` row this answer was billed to.

Returned so the answer is identifiable after the fact. Nothing can rate it
yet — `ai_response_feedbacks` is keyed on `ticket_message_id` and an ask
produces no message.

KnowledgeAskResponseDto.status.description: `null` only if the peer sent a member this build does not know.

KnowledgeGapsResponseDto.attachmentEmpty.description: The part of `emptyRetrievals` the rate above excludes.

KnowledgeGapsResponseDto.attachmentGroun.description: How many answering generations were given a file — reported, not hidden.

KnowledgeGapsResponseDto.emptyRetrievalR.description:
Over ATTACHMENT-FREE answering generations only.

`emptyRetrievals` above stays the total, so the two read together: a
question about a user's own file retrieved nothing correctly, and is not a
gap in the corpus.

KnowledgeSearchDto.skipRerank.description:
Returns what the RETRIEVER found, before the reranker had an opinion.

A diagnostic rather than a performance switch: a Knowledge Manager asking
"why isn't this document coming back" needs to know whether it lost at
retrieval or at rerank, and those are different problems with different
fixes.

KnowledgeSearchResponseDto.degraded.description:
Why this result set is thinner than usual, or `null` when it is not.

`LEXICAL_ONLY` means the vector search was skipped.

LockUserDto.lockedUntil.description:
When the lock should lapse.

**Absent means INDEFINITE**, which is the existing product and the default
an admin gets by not thinking about it.

**A PAST date is rejected**, not accepted. The database would take
it happily and the account would lock and unlock in the same instant —
legal, and incomprehensible to the admin who set it and the user who got
the email. Validated here and re-checked in auth-service, because the
gateway is not the only possible caller.

LockUserDto.reason.description:
Why the account is being locked. Required — it lands in the audit metadata
and in the email to the user.

LoginDto.deviceName.description:
Display label for the "your active sessions" screen ("Chrome on macOS").

Its destination is `device_sessions.device_name`, written when the session
row is created — which is why it looks unused in `login()`. Being
client-supplied, it must never influence a security decision: device trust
is proven with the separate `deviceToken` cookie, a secret the server
issued.

`@MaxLength(100)` mirrors `device_sessions.device_name VarChar(100)`;
without it an oversized value is a Postgres error on insert rather than a
400 at the edge.

Optional rather than nullable: absent means "the client did not label this
device", which is what the proto's `optional string` expects.

**There is deliberately no `ipAddress` field.** A body field is whatever
the client says it is, so accepting one would let an attacker post
`{"ipAddress": "10.0.0.1"}` to poison the audit trail and evade IP-based
lockout. The gateway derives it from the transport.

MarkReadResponseDto.countedAt.description: When `unreadCount` was counted, as on the unread count.

MarkReadResponseDto.unreadCount.description: Pushed back so a client never recomputes a badge it can be told.

MessageResponseDto.answerStatus.description:
What the generation concluded.

`null` for a human message, and also for a status this build cannot name.

MessageResponseDto.citations.description:
What an AI answer cited.

`null` for a human message and for an AI message written before citations
were stored; `[]` for an answer that cited nothing.

MessageResponseDto.excludedFromAiContext.description:
Kept OUT of AI prompts.

Exposed rather than stripped: the transcript builder in `AiStreamService`
filters on it AFTER fetching, because the same route serves the UI, where a
refused message stays visible.

MessageResponseDto.senderId.description: null for an AI-generated message — no user wrote it.

NotificationFeedResponseDto.nextCursor.description: null on the last page — a client that keeps polling gets nothing forever.

NotificationResponseDto.data.description: The event's payload, decoded from the JSON string the wire carries.

NotificationResponseDto.groupCount.description: "12 new messages on #1042" — how many events this row represents.

NotificationResponseDto.groupKey.description:
What collapses several events into one row — free-form, and deliberately
not an enum: the service composes it from a resource id.

NotificationResponseDto.priority.description: How urgent it is. `null` when the wire value is one this build cannot name.

NotificationResponseDto.resourceType.description: What the notification is ABOUT. `null` when unset or unrecognized.

NotificationResponseDto.type.description:
The ORIGINATING event — `ticket.assigned`, never the NATS subject.

`null` for a type this build does not recognise.

OrganizationResponseDto.status.description: `OrgStatus`, null when the bridge answers null for `UNSPECIFIED`

OrganizationSettingsResponseDto.inboundA.description:
The support address customers write to, `null` while inbound email is
off. A published address, not a secret: rotating it is how an old one
stops working.

OrganizationSettingsResponseDto.maxDocum.description:
What this workspace has configured, or `null` where it has configured
nothing.

`null` rather than the platform number: a screen that renders the ceiling
as if the tenant had chosen it cannot show the difference between an
inherited limit and a deliberate one, and the tenant would have no way to
tell whether clearing the field changes anything.

OrganizationSettingsResponseDto.publicDo.description: Accepted free-mail domains worth a second look. Never an error.

OrganizationUsageResponseDto.aiModelTier.description:
The plan, beside the meters

This is the page a customer opens when they hit a limit, and a limit with
no plan next to it is a number they cannot act on: the next question is
always "what would I get if I upgraded".

OrganizationUsageResponseDto.currentPeri.description: NULL for a grandfathered tenant, who has no invoice period at all.

OrganizationUsageResponseDto.storage.description:
Composed at the GATEWAY from ingestion's tenant-scoped usage read.

auth-service cannot answer it — it does not count documents and cannot dial
the service that does — so it sends this meter unavailable and the gateway
replaces it. `available: false` here therefore means the ingestion leg did
not answer, and never "this workspace has no storage".

The number is the one a plan-change refusal quotes. It has to be: a tenant
told to reduce storage opens this page to find out what to delete.

OverviewResponseDto.computedAt.description: When the rollups behind this answer ran.

OverviewResponseDto.dataThrough.description:
**The last day the rollups behind this answer cover**,
`YYYY-MM-DD`, or `null` when no rollup has ever run for this tenant.

Not the same as `computedAt`, and the gap between them is the diagnosis: a
recent `computedAt` beside a `dataThrough` two weeks old means the job runs
and finds nothing, while `dataThrough: null` means it has never run at all.
A dashboard of zeros looks identical in both cases without this field —
which is how seven scheduled jobs sat uncalled and nothing complained.

OverviewResponseDto.humanFirstResponseSe.description: Reported apart from the AI figure, always.

OverviewResponseDto.openTicketMedianAgeS.description:
The counterweight to `resolutionSeconds`, which can only see tickets that
closed and is therefore biased optimistic.

PageMeta.totalItems.description: Total matching records, across every page.

PaginationMetaDataResponseDto.itemCount.description: Records on THIS page — smaller than `itemsPerPage` on the last one.

PaginationMetaDataResponseDto.totalItems.description: Total matching records, across every page.

PermissionResponseDto.group.description: The `target` prefix of the code, for grouping in the role editor.

PermissionResponseDto.isRetired.description:
True when the code is in the table and no longer in `PERMISSION_CODES`.

Retired rather than deleted, because roles may still hold it (ADR 0038).
An editor should show it as ungrantable rather than as an option — the API
refuses it either way, and offering it makes the refusal read as a bug.

PlanChangeResponseDto.creditIssued.description:
Whether the proration credited rather than charged — **`null` when it could
not be determined.**

A downgrade produces a credit against future invoices, never a refund, and
a client that does not say so is a support ticket. Three-valued on purpose:
`always_invoice` does not guarantee the proration lands on the invoice this
is read from, so a `false` can be wrong for a change that credited and a
`true` can be read off an unrelated invoice. `null` means *say nothing* —
which is the honest option, and the one a comment on a plain `boolean`
cannot give a UI that is already rendering it.

PlanSubscriberProjectionResponseDto.afte.description:
The AFTER value of every NUMERIC column in `changes`, keyed the same way.

`changes` renders for a human; this is what a machine reads. A key absent
here means the column is not changing — never "zero", which would put every
tenant over. `aiModelTier` is a string and never appears.

known-gaps #21: the composer used to parse the display string, and a
cosmetic change to its separator silently disarmed two limit checks.

PlanSubscriberProjectionResponseDto.budg.description: Held to the next cycle roll: lowering a part-spent budget is retroactive.

PlanSubscriberProjectionResponseDto.chan.description: Field name → `"before -> after"`, for the columns this apply would change.

PlanSubscriberProjectionResponseDto.over.description:
Limits this tenant is ALREADY past under the new plan.

Reported, never enforced: a limit gates admission, never tenure. These
tenants keep everything they have and are refused their next addition.

The same limits as data, one per limit it breaks: what's in use against
what the new plan allows. The strings above stay one release.

PlanSubscriberProjectionResponseDto.skip.description: Off-catalogue by deliberate policy; this apply does not touch them.

PlatformOrganizationDetailResponseDto.bi.description:
Whether a Stripe subscription grants the plan: a limit edited by hand
then lasts until Stripe's next event. False for a plan assigned by hand.

PlatformOrganizationDetailResponseDto.pl.description: The catalogue plan it's on, or null when none is assigned.

PlatformOrganizationDetailResponseDto.st.description:
When the status last changed ("Frozen since"). Null for an organization
whose status changed before that was recorded.

PlatformOrganizationDetailResponseDto.us.description: Each meter is `READ_FAILED` when its service didn't answer; the page still loads.

PlatformOrganizationUsageResponseDto.aiT.description: This cycle's AI spend against the monthly allowance, in micros.

PlatformOrganizationUsageResponseDto.sea.description: Members plus pending invitations: the count the seat limit refuses on.

PlatformUserResponseDto.organizationId.description: Always present on a tenant user; null only for a platform Super Admin.

PreferenceResponseDto.digest.description: Whether matching notifications batch into a digest.

PreferenceResponseDto.source.description:
Where the value came from.

Lets the UI show "inherited" rather than presenting a default as a choice.

PreferenceResponseDto.type.description: The event this preference is for, or `'*'` for the catch-all row.

PresignAvatarDto.contentType.description:
No SVG. An SVG is a document that can carry script — the one image type
that behaves like an executable when served.

PresignDocumentDto.contentType.description: The document's MIME type. Must be one the parser accepts.

PreviewInvitationsResponseDto.seatOverru.description: Non-zero means the batch would be partially rejected at commit time.

RateResponseDto.rate.description: null when the denominator is zero — NOT zero. The two are different facts.

ReadinessResponseDto.draining.description: This instance is shutting down. Gates `ready`; see `DrainState`.

ReadinessResponseDto.peers.description: Peer connectivity, for humans during an incident. Does NOT gate.

ReplaceDocumentDto.objectPath.description: The object path, echoed back from the presign response.

ReplaceDocumentDto.ocrLanguages.description:
ISO 639-1 codes for OCR, if the uploader knows them.

Re-declared rather than inherited, and NOT carried over from the document
being replaced: reading a scan in the wrong language is one of the main
reasons to replace one, so the previous value is exactly what a caller may
be here to change. Absent means `[]`, which is the `eng` fallback — the
same meaning it has on confirm.

RequestOtpResponseDto.codeLength.description: How many digits the code has.

OtpStatusResponseDto.codeLength.description: How many digits a code has, pending or not.

RequestPhoneVerificationDto.phoneNumber.description:
Becomes `otps.target`. `users.phone_number` is not touched until a code for
this exact number verifies, which is what lets one endpoint serve both
first-time verification and change-of-number.

ResetPasswordResponseDto.revokedSessionC.description: Surfaced so the UI can say "you have been signed out of N devices".

RetrievedChunkResponseDto.pageNumber.description: NULL for formats with no pages — never faked as 1.

RetrievedChunkResponseDto.vectorPointId.description: The id a citation resolves through, and the two arms' fusion key.

RoleResponseDto.isSystemRole.description: Readable by every tenant, mutable by none.

SessionResponseDto.current.description: The session this request arrived on, matched by family — not by IP.

SetDocumentDepartmentsDto.departmentIds.description:
The FULL replacement set, not a delta.

Replacement rather than add/remove because the fan-out ordering (
The fan-out ordering turns on whether a change restricts, and that is answerable from a
before/after pair but not from a stream of deltas applied in unknown order.

SetOrganizationStatusDto.reason.description: Required — the audit row is read months later by someone who was not there.

enforces it, because zero is as invalid as two.

StartConversationDto.message.description: The opening question. Becomes the ticket's description.

StartConversationDto.attachments.description:
The question's files, already uploaded through
`POST /tickets/attachments/upload-url`. Bound before the first answer is
asked for, so the answer reads them. A path that fails its confirm comes
back in `skippedAttachments`; the conversation starts regardless.

SubmitFeedbackDto.citationAccurate.description:
Whether the citations the model gave were accurate.

Tri-state on purpose — absent means "not assessed", which is different from
"assessed and wrong". Collapsing the two would make every un-assessed reply
look like a citation failure in the quality report.

SubmitFeedbackDto.rating.description: A thumb: `1` for up, `-1` for down.

SubscriptionPlanPriceResponseDto.interva.description:
The billing period this price charges for — `month` or `year` in practice.

Not narrowed to those two: the value is whatever Stripe sent, and Stripe's
own vocabulary includes `day` and `week`.

SubscriptionPlanPriceResponseDto.stripeP.description: Stripe's id. `month` and `year` on one plan are the reason this is a list.

SubscriptionPlanPriceResponseDto.unitAmo.description:
What Stripe charges, in the currency's smallest unit (cents for `usd`).
Read from Stripe when the plan is created; null for a price stored before
amounts were.

SubscriptionPlanResponseDto.maxAnalytics.description: Days of history analytics may look back over. Narrowing it is retroactive.

SubscriptionPlanResponseDto.stripeProduc.description: NULL for a plan ASSIGNED rather than sold — the negotiated agreement.

SubscriptionPlanResponseDto.subscriberCo.description: Live tenants on this plan: the delete gate and the apply's blast radius.

SubscriptionResponseDto.planName.description: A label. Never an authorization input.

SubscriptionResponseDto.status.description:
`OrgStatus` — **ours, not Stripe's**, despite living on a subscription
response. The proto field is `OrgStatus` and its comment says so: *"the
tenant lifecycle status the subscription drove"*. Only the neighbouring
`InvoiceResponseDto.status` carries Stripe's vocabulary.

SubscriptionResponseDto.stripeCustomerId.description: NULL for a grandfathered tenant — free, internal, or pre-billing.

SuggestedArticleResponseDto.pageNumber.description: `null` for a source with no pages — a pasted text file, an HTML article.

SuggestedArticleResponseDto.score.description: How well it matched, so a client can show or sort by relevance.

TenantPlanPriceResponseDto.interval.description: Stripe's literal — `month` | `year` in practice, and wider in theory.

TicketResponseDto.ticketNumber.description: A number, not a string: `longs: Number` keeps int64 exact to 2^53.

TicketResponseDto.unreadCount.description:
Messages the caller has not read on this ticket.

Excludes their own and any internal note they cannot see. A ticket never
opened counts as ALL unread, not zero. Always `0` on a single-ticket read —
a badge is a list affordance, and a caller looking at one ticket is reading
it.

TicketResponseDto.attachments.description:
The files uploaded with the ticket's opening (the description); empty
when none. A message's files are on the message.

TicketStatusActionDto.reason.description: Why the ticket moved. Recorded on the status history and visible to agents; the ticket author sees only reasons they wrote themselves.

TicketStatusChangeResponseDto.fromStatus.description: Null on a row with no prior status.

TicketStatusChangeResponseDto.reason.description: Null when the caller may not read it — see the route's docblock.

TwoFactorEnabledResponseDto.backupCodes.description: Shown once. Only hashes are stored.

TwoFactorEnabledResponseDto.user.description: The user signed in when two-step was enabled through the sign-in challenge; null when it was enabled from a session.

TwoFactorRequiredResponseDto.canRemember.description:
Whether "remember this device" can skip the next code: false for a Super
Admin, who is asked every time, so the page hides the option.

TwoFactorRequiredResponseDto.requiresTwo.description:
True when two-step is REQUIRED and this account has not enrolled: its
organization requires it, or the account is a Super Admin (who always
must, and whose device is never remembered).

The client must branch on it: `false` means prompt for a code, `true` means
open the enrolment screen and call `POST /auth/2fa/setup` — which accepts
the challenge cookie precisely for this case. Showing a code box here would
ask for a code that does not exist yet, which is how a tenant-wide
`enforce_two_factor` becomes a tenant-wide lockout.

UnavailableBlockResponseDto.source.description: Which leg failed, by service name.

UnreadCountResponseDto.countedAt.description:
When the database counted it (ISO 8601). A client keeps the newest count
it has, from any answer, refetch or push, and drops an older one that
arrives later.

UploadAttachmentDto.fileSizeBytes.description:
Declared by the client and therefore not trustworthy on its own — the real

earns its place: it turns "upload 2 GB, then be refused" into an immediate
refusal, and it documents the cap in the API contract.

UploadAttachmentDto.mimeType.description:
An allowlist, never a denylist. A denylist is a promise to have thought of
every dangerous type, which is not a promise anyone can keep.

UsageMeterResponseDto.unavailableReason.description:

couldn't be read just now; try again) or `NOT_AVAILABLE` (this
organization has no such meter). Null when available.

UserResponseDto.dob.description:
Date of birth as ISO `YYYY-MM-DD` — a calendar date, with no time and no
zone. `null` when the user has not given one.

UserResponseDto.lockedUntil.description:

Render on `isLocked`; read this to show *when* the lock ends.

UserResponseDto.organizationId.description:

UserSummaryResponseDto.deletedAt.description: Non-null only on a deactivated account.

WebhookEndpointResponseDto.disabledReaso.description:

WebhookEndpointResponseDto.eventTypes.description:

WebhookEndpointWithSecretResponseDto.sec.description: `whsec_…` — store it now; no read returns it again.

TicketResponseDto.department.description: The department the ticket is in, resolved from `currentDepartmentId`. Null when it is in none, or when it could not be resolved: auth-service did not answer, or the id names nobody (a deleted user or department). A client shows "Unknown" for it.

MessageResponseDto.sender.description: Who wrote the message, resolved from `senderId`. Always null for an AI-generated message: no user wrote it. PresignAttachmentResponseDto.uploadMetho.description:

SubscriptionResponseDto.currentPeriodEnd.description:
